question: What is the primary purpose of health advocacy in community nursing?

options.A: Prescribing medications during rural community outreaches
options.B: Managing hospital finances and administrative staff schedules
options.C: Speaking up for vulnerable populations to secure health resources
options.D: Conducting laboratory tests in primary health centers

explanation: Health advocacy centers on protecting patient rights and securing necessary resources for those who cannot easily speak for themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h1)

question: A community health nurse advocates for a marginalized group primarily because...

options.A: nurses have legal immunity when challenging local government decisions
options.B: hospitals require community consent before admitting emergency cases
options.C: these groups often face barriers that limit access to quality healthcare
options.D: the government pays extra allowances for community outreach programs

explanation: Vulnerable groups frequently encounter systemic hurdles like poverty and poor infrastructure, necessitating nurse intervention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h1)

question: Which advocacy principle focuses on fair distribution of health resources?
explanation: Social justice ensures that health resources are distributed equitably without discrimination against vulnerable groups. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h2)

question: Empowerment as an advocacy value means helping community members to...

options.A: fund local primary healthcare clinics through community taxes
options.B: rely entirely on the nurse for all future health decisions
options.C: enforce health legislation without government supervision
options.D: build the confidence to speak up for their own health needs

explanation: Empowering communities fosters self-reliance so they can champion their own health causes independently. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h2)

question: When a nurse explains health rights to villagers using local language, what role is being displayed?
explanation: The educator role involves breaking down complex health concepts and rights so community members can easily understand them. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h3)

question: A nurse intervenes upon discovering a primary clinic is denying care to indigent pregnant women. Which advocate role is this?
explanation: Acting as a protector involves stepping in directly to safeguard vulnerable patients from exploitation and unfair treatment. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h3)

question: What is the first step a nurse should take before launching an advocacy campaign?

options.A: Filing a formal lawsuit against the local government
options.B: Assessing community health needs and gathering data
options.C: Closing down non-compliant primary health centers
options.D: Ordering expensive medical equipment from abroad

explanation: Data collection and needs assessment ensure that advocacy efforts target real, pressing problems in the community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h4)

question: Why is analyzing local morbidity and mortality records crucial for health advocacy?

options.A: It reveals the specific diseases causing the most harm in the area
options.B: It determines the monthly salary of primary healthcare workers
options.C: It helps the nurse predict the weather patterns for outreach days
options.D: It satisfies international travel requirements for nurses

explanation: Morbidity and mortality data highlight clear health disparities and burdens facing the target population. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h4)

question: Which communication skill helps a nurse truly understand community grievances?
explanation: Active listening ensures that the nurse captures the real concerns and feelings of community members. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h5)

question: Why should a nurse frame health advocacy arguments around shared community benefits?

options.A: It eliminates the need to collect baseline health statistics
options.B: It guarantees automatic promotion for the community health nurse
options.C: It persuades reluctant stakeholders by showing how everyone gains
options.D: It prevents the government from auditing hospital financial records

explanation: Connecting health improvements to broader community benefits like economic productivity gains stronger stakeholder support. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h5)

question: Who can provide valuable cultural and community backing for health initiatives in Nigeria?
explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold immense influence and can rally community support for public health programs. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h6)

question: Why must a nurse understand local government administrative channels during advocacy?

options.A: To avoid paying taxes on personal nursing equipment
options.B: To qualify for appointment as a local government chairperson
options.C: To know the right offices and officials responsible for health funding
options.D: To bypass all medical ethics committees during clinical trials

explanation: Knowing administrative channels ensures that advocacy messages and budget requests reach the actual decision-makers. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h6)

question: What is a common fear that discourages nurses from speaking out against unsafe conditions?

options.A: Fear of institutional victimization or job loss
options.B: Fear of receiving excess clinical allowances
options.C: Fear of winning too many international awards
options.D: Fear of mandatory retirement at age thirty

explanation: Fear of administrative backlash and victimization often silences health workers who witness substandard practices. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h7)

question: Which strategy best protects a nurse facing ethical dilemmas during advocacy work?

options.A: Relying on documented evidence and professional association backing
options.B: Resigning immediately without notifying any colleagues
options.C: Spreading unverified rumors on social media platforms
options.D: Refusing to document any clinical errors in the hospital ward

explanation: Solid evidence and the collective strength of professional bodies provide a safety shield for advocating nurses. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h7)
